h: Vows Become Sacred When Speech Expresses the Divine Will

p: "And Moshe spoke to the heads of the tribes
of the Children of Yisrael, saying:
זֶה הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה ה׳ (בְּמִדְבַּר ל, ב)
This is the thing that Hashem commanded" (Bamidbar 30:2).
In the Gemara (Nedarim 78a) it is found
is written to teach about an expert individual.
Now this needs to be understood:
if it is to indicate an expert individual,
why are "the heads of the tribes" mentioned?
After all, there were in Yisrael
and all of them were experts;
specifically the heads of the tribes?
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁמָּצִינוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
based on what we find in the holy Zohar
(at the beginning of the introduction to the Tikkunim),
and lists "heads" as corresponding to Kesser Elyon.
Now, in the passage of vows
the expression "this is the thing" is written,
which indicates that this is the word of Hashem,
along the lines of what is said in the Sifrei (Matos 1):
in that he prophesied with 'this is the thing'";
meaning that these are the very words
that come forth from the mouth of Hashem Yisbarach;
the Shechinah speaks from within his throat.
he has vowed a nazirite vow and an offering, etc."
for it is the way of the wicked to vow.
"In all my days I never ate
the guilt-offering of a defiled nazir, etc.;
My son, may there be many like you
that he intended only for the sake of Heaven,
and it was the will of Hashem Yisbarach
that he fence himself in with nezirus;
that he intends it for the sake of Heaven,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּירוּשַׁלְמִי פֶּרֶק ט דִּנְדָרִים
as is written in the Yerushalmi, chapter 9 of Nedarim (9:1):
"Is it not enough for you what the Torah forbade,
And therefore the expression mentioned here is
"this is the thing that Hashem commanded":
that the word that comes forth from his mouth be
along the lines of what the holy Zohar says
and it is the mouth of Hashem,
the aspect of "Malchus is the mouth,"
וְהוּא דְּבָרַי אֲשֶׁר שַׂמְתִּי בְּפִיךָ (יְשַׁעְיָהוּ נט, כא)
and it is "My words that I have put in your mouth" (Yeshayahu 59:21).
Then the word that comes forth from his mouth
and for him the vow is a mitzvah.
And this is why it is mentioned here,
at the beginning of this parsha,
who correspond to the attribute of Kesser Elyon,
and Kesser Elyon is the crown of Malchus;
and to them the matter of vows was handed over,
the time and the place that are fitting
to make a fence and a vow;
וְאָז יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת דְּבַר ה׳ מַמָּשׁ
and then it can be truly the word of Hashem
"this is the thing that Hashem commanded";
And this is the matter of
what is said in the Midrash
(רַבָּא וְתַנְחוּמָא רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה כב, א)
(Rabbah and Tanchuma at the beginning of this parsha, Bamidbar Rabbah 22:1):
you are not permitted to swear
אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ תִּירָא (דְּבָרִים ו, יג)
for Torah and for occupying yourself with mitzvos,
and you have no other occupation."
that his word be the mouth of Hashem,
which is from the dew of Atika.
But for one who cannot be
among those who toil in Torah,
it says "and for occupying yourself with mitzvos";
and this is based on what is written by
"And all your deeds shall be for the sake of Heaven"
in the affairs of this world,
rather, everything is an act of mitzvah.
But it must be in such a way
that you have no business at all
except with intent for the sake of Heaven.
this is along the lines of
מָצָאתִי לָהֶן תַּקָּנָה מִן הַתּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵּי
I have found a remedy for them from the Torah, etc.;
but is it possible to cleave to the Shechinah? etc.;
כָּל הַמַּשִּׂיא בִּתּוֹ לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם וְכוּלֵּי
whoever marries his daughter to a Torah scholar, etc.,
as if he cleaves to the Shechinah";
And they said there in the Midrash:
אִם יֵשׁ בְּךָ כָּל הַמִּדּוֹת הָאֵלּוּ
And this is why it is written
"and by His Name shall you swear (tishave'a)" (Devarim 6:13)
that he will be bound by an oath through the Name
and will not transgress his word;
for then the word that comes forth from his mouth
and it will surely enter the heart,
וְלֹא יַעֲבוֹר עַל זֶה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
and he will not transgress it, Heaven forbid.
"May there be many like you who vow nezirus in Yisrael";
he was concerned that they would regret it,
and so for them it applies:
טוֹב אֲשֶׁר לֹא תִדּוֹר (קֹהֶלֶת ה, ד)
"It is better that you not vow" (Koheles 5:4),
and one who vows is as if he built a private altar;
and as is written in the Yerushalmi:
לֹא דַיֶּיךָ בְּמַה שֶּׁאָסְרָה תּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵּי
"Is it not enough for you what the Torah forbade, etc.";
that he will transgress his vow.
who intended for the sake of Heaven:
he will certainly not regret it
וְלֹא יַעֲבוֹר חַס וְשָׁלוֹם עַל נִדְרוֹ
and will not, Heaven forbid, transgress his vow;
and for him the vow and the oath are a mitzvah.
"and by His Name shall you swear";
that he will be bound by the oath
the passage of vows was said.
כָּמוֹךָ יִרְבּוּ נוֹזְרֵי נְזִירוּת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּלֵּי
"May there be many like you who vow nezirus in Yisrael, etc."
And so we find regarding an oath:
"I have sworn, and I will fulfill it, etc." (Tehillim 119:106)
and this applies to one who has
who is assured that he will be bound by the oath
who sees his inclination overpowering him,
and fences himself in and binds himself by oath
this too is the word of Hashem,
as is written, "and by His Name shall you swear":
so that he will not transgress.
